verses.text: Now I have something to say to the church leaders among you. I am a leader too, and I saw Christ suffer with my own eyes. I will also share in the glory that will be shown. I beg you:

take care of God's flock, the people in your care, like shepherds. Watch over them, not because you have to, but because you want to, as God wants. Do not do it to get money, but because you are eager to serve.
Do not boss around the people in your care, but be good examples to them.
When Christ, the Chief Shepherd, appears, you will receive a crown of glory that will never fade away.
In the same way, you younger people should accept the authority of the leaders. All of you, be humble with each other, because "God is against the proud, but he is kind to the humble."
So humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, and at the right time he will lift you up.
Give all your worries to him, because he cares about you.
Keep a clear head and control yourselves. Stay alert! Your enemy the devil walks around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to eat.
Stand against him, and stay strong in your faith. Remember that your brothers and sisters all over the world are going through the same kind of suffering.

You will suffer for a little while. But after that, God, who is full of kindness and who called you to share his glory forever in Christ Jesus, will make you complete and strong. He will hold you up and keep you steady.
All power belongs to him forever and ever. Amen.
I have written this short letter with the help of Silas, who I know is a faithful brother. I want to encourage you and tell you that this is the true kindness of God. Stand firm in it.
The church here in Babylon, chosen by God just like you, sends you greetings. So does my son Mark.
Greet each other with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who belong to Christ. Amen.
